**Tenant Isolation:**
- Queries on org- or project-owned rows (DAL files under backend/src/services and backend/src/ee/services) that do not filter by the orgId or projectId of the authenticated actor
- Lookups by ID that return a row from another organization or project because the scope check happens after the read, or not at all
- Machine identity or service token paths that resolve resources outside the token's own org or project

**Authorization:**
- New or changed routes and service methods that act on a resource without a permissionService.getProjectPermission / getOrgPermission call followed by ForbiddenError.from(permission).throwUnlessCan(...) for the action actually performed
- Returning a secret value when only DescribeSecret was checked; value reads require ReadValue (see hasSecretReadValueOrDescribePermission)
- Returning a stored credential, certificate private key, or KMS key material when only the "use" action was checked; the read or export action must be enforced on its own
- Role, privilege, or membership changes that do not go through assertRoleSetBoundary / validatePrivilegeChangeOperation
- Permission resolution that skips isActiveRole, letting an expired temporary role or privilege still apply
- New CASL condition operators or glob handling that change how isOperatorsASubset or validatePermissionBoundary compare rules

**Authentication:**
- Routes that drop or loosen onRequest: verifyAuth([...]), accept an AuthMode the handler does not expect, or add the deprecated API_KEY or SERVICE_TOKEN modes to new code
- Changes to backend/src/server/plugins/auth (inject-identity, verify-auth, inject-assume-privilege) that let a request proceed without a verified identity
- Machine identity auth methods (OIDC, JWT, Kubernetes, AWS, Azure, GCP, SPIFFE, LDAP) that skip signature, issuer, audience, or bound-claim verification on the external assertion
- SAML, OIDC, or LDAP login paths that skip assertion signature or replay checks

**Secrets and Cryptography:**
- Secret values, tokens, keys, or credentials persisted without encryption through the KMS service (createCipherPairWithDataKey) or the lib/crypto helpers. Report these even though the general exclusions skip secrets stored on disk: that exclusion assumes encryption at rest, which this code skips.
- New hand-rolled encryption, static or reused IVs or nonces, or key material shared across orgs or projects
- Token, HMAC, or signature comparisons that do not use a constant-time comparison
- Secret values, access tokens, encryption keys, or request bodies carrying them written to logs, error messages, audit log metadata, or telemetry
- Sensitive fields (encrypted blobs, hashes, private keys, tokens) added to a route's Zod response schema

**Server-Side Request Forgery:**
- New HTTP requests to user-supplied URLs (webhooks, app connections, secret syncs, rotations, dynamic secrets, integrations) that do not go through safeRequest from backend/src/lib/validator/safe-request.ts
- Redirect handling on user-supplied URLs that follows a redirect without validating and pinning the next hop

**Secret References, Imports, and Sharing:**
- Same-project secret reference expansion that resolves a secret in another environment or folder without the canExpandValue check
- Cross-project references or imports that resolve without a matching project folder grant, ignore the organization's cross-project sharing setting, or resolve across organizations
- Secret sharing links with guessable tokens, or that skip their expiry, max-views, or organization restriction checks

**Database Migrations:**
- Migrations under backend/src/db/migrations that read the license service or a feature flag, directly or through a helper (for example getMigrationEncryptionServices without skipHsmLicenseCheck: true); the license is not initialized when migrations run, so the migration can take the wrong encryption path. Report these even with no attacker involved, since they can corrupt or expose encrypted data.

**CI Workflows:**
- Workflows triggered by pull_request_target or workflow_run that check out or execute code from the pull request
- PR-controlled values (title, body, branch name, commit message) interpolated with ${{ }} directly into a run: script
